name_intro: {name} {pronunciation} is a misspelling of the German {kaliber}, itself the root of the English word {calibre}, as in "high-calibre". that is deliberate: that's how you know i {own} the app.
libre: also, the "libre" part of the name actually means as it does in {libre}: free referring to liberty, not cost like free beer.
libre_aside: (although, it technically also is free in cost.)
shorthand: the official shorthand {kb} doubles as the obvious abbreviation for {keyboard}. that felt right for a tool built around one.
exist_intro: {name} started as a personal project, a way to train on the specific mistakes i kept making, and the mistakes i {would} make, rather than running the same drills. the mistake map, the adaptive drilling, the sustained accuracy mode: all of it came from wanting something that learned {my} patterns.
exist_dev: i use it in development too, beyond testing features 'cause typing through something i already wrote is a good way to sit with it.
fun_fact_text: i actually enjoy typing tests in sustained mode!
